prompt_en: A photographic space-horror scene: a woman whose facial appearance and short dark bob are guided by the supplied portrait stands in an unsettling encounter inside the listening nursery of a living spacecraft. The supplied portrait guides her face and hair, while her work clothes and surroundings belong to this invented scene. Her large brown eyes, delicate oval face and wispy dark fringe remain recognizable in a clear three-quarter view. She wears a pale gray expedition coverall with a small amber work lamp at the sternum. Her lips are slightly parted as she looks down toward the nearest organism, her unguarded face warm and human against the chamber. She has stopped halfway through a careful step on a narrow maintenance landing. Her left boot is planted flat on the deck; her right boot hovers a few centimeters above it, knee softly bent. Her left hand grips the waist-high rail beside her, and her right hand stays close against her chest. The interrupted movement reads as a person suddenly realizing that this place can notice her. The inner hull forms broad pale cartilage arches joined by taut semitranslucent membranes with branching dark vessels. A manufactured circular porthole is set into one living arch, its bolted metal ring clasped by the membrane; through it, a sparse star field and the hard white edge of a distant moon establish the spacecraft's exterior. The deck and arch membranes meet in continuous grown folds, giving the structure the material continuity of an organ rather than decoration applied to a room. Beside the landing, a shallow black nursery pool supports a small colony of unfamiliar sail organisms. Each has a dark knotted holdfast fixed to the pool bed, a thin stalk and a broad translucent fan with fine radiating ribs. Three large near fans curve toward the woman's hovering boot, their wet edges close to the landing; two distant fans remain upright deeper in the pool. Tiny pale cilia form a fringe at the near holdfasts. These are separate organisms living within the vessel, distinct from the large structural hull arches. Her hovering boot, the nearest bending fans and their rooted bases are visible together across one diagonal gap. Compose a landscape 3:2 photograph from the landing at a slightly low three-quarter viewpoint. Her full figure fills the left foreground, the nearest colony fills the lower right, and the porthole stays readable above the pool. The amber lamp illuminates her face and catches the organisms' ribbed translucency; cold diffused blue from the porthole separates the hull membranes. Controlled shadows retain the stalks, holdfasts and rail grip. Set the depth of field so her face and the near colony's fan-stalk-holdfast chains stay sharply readable together, while the far hull softens gently with distance. Detailed photographic skin, worn fabric, wet thin membranes and mineral residue give the impossible habitat convincing physical presence. The dominant feeling is the quiet instant before she dares lower her foot.

h_f2_material_decisions.rationale: S00; Layered enclosing membranes overlap the authored hull, but the complete Cosmic womb source additionally requires small niches embedded in its membrane. That distinctive cavity-membrane-niche cue has no native qualification here; I do not retrofit it or claim the existing porthole equals many niches. No distinct admissible whole-cue alternative is available. See composition-comparison.md#source-s00.

S01; The full source is an outdoor bathing pool opening to outdoor space with continuous wet coping. The nursery pool is inside a spacecraft, and the porthole does not make it outdoors. Using only the wet edge would discard its named outdoor relationship. See composition-comparison.md#source-s01.

S02; The source requires orbital-human-operations primary context and an exterior EVA worksite with hull curvature, handrails, service panels and open space. Those frozen primary facts are absent. A window showing stars is not an exterior worksite. See composition-comparison.md#source-s02.

S03; The complete source specifies an explicitly adult EVA worker in a pressure suit, helmet, life-support backpack and tether outside a vehicle. No frozen adult or exterior EVA fact exists; a full helmet also hides facial/hair guidance. I do not borrow only the expedition role from that whole source. See composition-comparison.md#source-s03.

S04; World-parent-separation context and near-touching sky/earth around a widening central interval are required. The nursery has a real pool and continuous hull, not a cosmogonic sky/earth separation. General enclosing curves are insufficient. See composition-comparison.md#source-s04.

S05; V01 requires inner and separate outer hatches bounding one short chamber, a suited crew member inside, and the outer hatch open to exterior. It affects subject as well as appearance/count/pose/setting. The current subject lock and absent hatch owners cannot support whole-source adoption; the porthole is not an outer hatch. Exposed new space-horror source, unused. See composition-comparison.md#source-s05.

S06; The glacier source requires crevassed active ice, lateral moraine and broad valley walls in one natural valley. Those linked owners cannot be imported as a local nursery detail; pale hull arches do not establish ice or geological flow. See composition-comparison.md#source-s06.

S07; A walker resting beside a connected route on a bench/low wall is a possible local change, realized completely as ALT_REST. Compared with the arrested-step baseline, its more settled support weakens the immediate boot-colony question. Final retains the suspended step. See composition-comparison.md#source-s07.

S08; One leg providing principal support with the free leg unloaded and torso above the base is already materially realized by the planted left boot, hovering right boot and rail grip. The source does not require a new gesture, and no candidate-driven change is retained. See composition-comparison.md#source-s08.

S09; This profile is a fictional body slumping into its own connected pool with upper structure losing support. The nursery pool is separate from the human, and no such owned melting mechanism is in the core. It would introduce a new focal bodily transformation and cannot be adopted from this unqualified discovery profile. See composition-comparison.md#source-s09.

S10; Retire requires the working foot near the support knee, a folded opened knee and visible support foot. That is a dance-like held configuration rather than the few-centimeter step and would move the boot far from the nearest fans. Its human prerequisite does not supply native whole-cue permission; no part of its distinctive pose is retained. See composition-comparison.md#source-s10.

S11; The bundle requires a visibly thick sole under forefoot and heel on one boot; it has an optional child but no native adoption authority here. An independently generic thick-sole choice is compared in ALT_FOOTWEAR. Its mass distracts from the delicate raised-foot relationship, so it is not used. See composition-comparison.md#source-s11.

S12; The S-curve source explicitly requires adult and human primary tags, an adult planted-foot weight shift, offset pelvis/shoulders and connected restrained curved axis. Adulthood is not frozen from the portrait, and a general graceful posture cannot satisfy that source prerequisite. See composition-comparison.md#source-s12.

S13; The old-growth forest requires canopy layers, a gap, snags and fallen logs. The nursery is not a forest; the fan colony and hull arches cannot substitute for those complete environmental owners. See composition-comparison.md#source-s13.

S14; The bundle is soft shaft folds settling above the same boot ankle, with an optional child. A generic fabric fold refinement is compared in ALT_FOOTWEAR, without adopting the bundle. It adds costume rhythm but no meaningful ecological information, so it is unused. See composition-comparison.md#source-s14.

S15; The complete forefoot-contact/raised-heel/opposite-planted-foot configuration is compared as ALT_CONTACT using generic positive geometry. It is physically clear, but gives a waiting stance instead of a step suddenly arrested above the deck. The original hovering boot is retained; the bundle is unselected. See composition-comparison.md#source-s15.

S16; Kelp requires a substrate attachment, continuous stipes to broad blades and coherent underwater orientations. The independently written organisms have holdfast-stalk-fan continuity already, but their sails are air-exposed above a shallow pool and deliberately differ in near/far orientation. I do not rename them kelp or silently discard the underwater scope. See composition-comparison.md#source-s16.

S17; This coral profile requires connected skeletal colony forms, sufficiently scaled polyps and water between branches. The living sails are separate thin fan organisms rather than a branched skeleton. Adding only a coral-like texture would omit the selected profile components; it remains unselected. See composition-comparison.md#source-s17.

S18; Crop-failure comparison requires a blackened drooping strip bordering upright green crop rows within the same field. Near leaning and far upright fans are not damaged crops. I preserve the exact difference and do not turn orientation into a disease or blight claim. See composition-comparison.md#source-s18.

S19; The focus source is explicitly near eye plus farther physical flower plane with softer petal boundaries, gated to portrait/flower context. There are no physical flowers; fans are not petals. Its full owner-specific relation is unused; the separate generic environmental-depth source informs ALT_FOCUS. See composition-comparison.md#source-s19.

S20; V64 requires a lone crew member at frame edge beside a lit doorway, long empty corridor and broad unlit viewport, with no visible creature. It affects subject and requires a linked architectural closure absent here. Treating its emptiness as an addition would remove the independent ecology scene; no whole-source authority is granted. Exposed new space-horror source, unused. See composition-comparison.md#source-s20.

S21; The profile joins transparent tail bases to a visible external waist support, a costume relation. Sail stalks attached to holdfasts are not costume tails, and the portrait-guided woman has no such support. It remains unselected rather than borrowing transparent material alone. See composition-comparison.md#source-s21.

S22; The source distinguishes a crisp subject plane, recognizable middle environmental forms and far-background detail loss. ALT_FOCUS compares a generic photographic depth refinement, selected for the literal final clause: Set the depth of field so her face and the near colony's fan-stalk-holdfast chains stay sharply readable together, while the far hull softens gently with distance. Whole-source/native adoption is declined; this is independently justified optical planning on open camera scope, with no new owner or hard gate. See composition-comparison.md#source-s22.

S23; V03 requires a ragged through-hole in a spacecraft shell, black exterior beyond and insulation fragments suspended beside the torn edge; it affects body geometry and setting relations. The intact bolted porthole is not damage, and adding a breach would change the gravity/air context that supports the step and pool. No source-owned mechanism is imported. Exposed new space-horror source, unused. See composition-comparison.md#source-s23.

S24; Two gathered side buns contradict the preserved supplied-portrait short dark bob. The requester reference-use anchor stays literal, so this hair source cannot be used even though it was returned for the word space. See composition-comparison.md#source-s24.

S25; The horror-comedy source needs an explicitly adult actor calmly labelling a fictional monstrous prop at a shared workstation dominated by that object. Adult fact, prop/workstation and labelling task are absent. A calm face alone is not its task-threat contrast. See composition-comparison.md#source-s25.

S26; Concept object photography centers an object/product approach. The reference-guided woman and her embodied encounter are the focal subject; converting the frame to an object study would demote the required reference use rather than provide a useful local style change. See composition-comparison.md#source-s26.

S27; The broad horror portrait genre is already realized by the opening space-horror photograph and warm human face within a threatening alien chamber. It provides no additional concrete relation or distinctive compatible change, so it is not credited as new source use. See composition-comparison.md#source-s27.

S28; An e-waste survey photograph is a documentary anchor for discarded electronics. The pool ecology is not e-waste and no robot provenance is requested. This empty-effect record supplies no usable local relationship. See composition-comparison.md#source-s28.

S29; Labyrinth-set contrast describes repeated set boundaries and human/clothing readability, with an adult-and-set owner relation. No adult fact is frozen and a repeated maze would introduce a different spatial premise. Existing single landing and reference face remain clearer; no fragment is relabelled as that complete contrast. See composition-comparison.md#source-s29.

S30; The drowning-imagery source requires a clearly adult clothed figure below water, a surface above and a distant ladder beyond. It affects subject as well as pose/count/relationship. No adult fact or submerged-human event is frozen; the pool is beside the woman, not over her. These owners cannot be reassigned. See composition-comparison.md#source-s30.

S31; A landing-page hero image is an output-use/style designation with no visible scene relation. There is no page brief or text-safe layout requirement, so it adds no justified local photographic change. See composition-comparison.md#source-s31.

S32; The high-key profile has five cumulative tonal requirements, with native/both/thumbnail gates and excluded substitutes. It has no native qualification and is not selected. ALT_BRIGHT compares only the independent generic choice of a brighter membrane-lit chamber; its clinical clarity is outweighed by weaker human/colony hierarchy. See composition-comparison.md#source-s32.

S33; The specimen source requires a separate irregular sample resting on an inner pedestal inside a transparent vessel, with a gap to the wall. The nursery pool is open and its holdfasts are living bases, not a pedestal in a vessel. A literal sealed specimen display would create a different containment relation, not clarify the current ecology. See composition-comparison.md#source-s33.

S34; The oceanpunk manifold requires oceanpunk primary context, seals, oxygen-loop gauge, sacrificial corrosion hardware, tidal coupling and a resident replacing a worn part. The living ship has no such loop, marine condition or replacement action. A work lamp or rail cannot substitute for that system. See composition-comparison.md#source-s34.

S35; The hime-cut profile cumulatively requires long rear hair, two blunt cheek/jaw panels and disconnected length steps readable together. The reference-guided short bob has no long rear mass; adopting it would alter the required reference-use meaning. It remains unselected. See composition-comparison.md#source-s35.

S36; The towel source requires both hands on one taut upper edge, continuous torso/pelvis cover and a separate swimsuit behind with a strap window. The acting rail hand and expedition coverall belong to a different event. Borrowing drape alone would discard the whole cloth/swimsuit relation; no change is retained. See composition-comparison.md#source-s36.

S37; The closed bodily carrier, its enclosing translucent membrane and multiple oval inner silhouettes are a distinctive incubation proxy. The independent hull membrane and fans do not already establish that host/inner-form relation. It is unqualified and would shift the encounter to a new gestation motif; no part is adopted as evidence of reproduction. See composition-comparison.md#source-s37.

S38; The distant-silhouette source specifies one small distant human, a large lit hall and broad empty floor interval; its subject effects are closed. Rendering the focal woman as a small distant silhouette would also prevent the requested face/hair guidance from being observable. A second figure is not licensed by that source and is not added. See composition-comparison.md#source-s38.

S39; The low-key profile requires all five relations: deliberate dark dominance, coherent selectively lit planes, differentiated shadow densities, controlled highlights and correctly exposed lit detail. The baseline has practical warm/cold light and retained shadow clues, but does not establish the complete profile. It remains unselected; no blanket darkening or hidden extra gate is added. See composition-comparison.md#source-s39.

semantic_clarification_decisions.rationale: Preserve the frozen reference-guided human and space-horror encounter; all four narrow requester anchor phrases remain literal. Nursery structure, organism shape, costume and halted-step staging remain authorial choices.

authorial_decisions.decision: Keep the reference face and complete near organism chains readable together through explicit optical depth.
authorial_decisions.rationale: ALT_FOCUS improves simultaneous observation more directly than extra costume detail, resting stance or brighter general illumination. It preserves the independent encounter and all requester anchors.

sensual.artistic_interpretation: The unguarded warmly lit face, parted lips and arrested graceful movement support a subtle human attraction within the uneasy scene. The portrayal is led by the encounter rather than a separate body focus.

adult_appeal_brief.contextual_comparison: No axis-specific candidates were returned. Compare the same sensual=1 baseline human presence across ALT_FOCUS, ALT_FOOTWEAR, ALT_CONTACT, ALT_REST and ALT_BRIGHT. ALT_FOCUS retains intimate human warmth while helping the habitat relation read; added costume detail and clinical brightness are less useful.

I rechecked the one woman, rail reach, leg support, separate organism chains and porthole view together. No introduced object or contact changes physical ownership. This is authored preflight, not pixel evidence.
